**Operation Car Wash (Lava Jato) and Petrobras**
A massive corruption investigation launched in 2014 that uncovered a bribery and money-laundering scheme in which construction firms paid kickbacks to politicians and executives at Petrobras, Brazil's state-controlled oil company, headquartered in Rio de Janeiro. It implicated politicians across parties and helped bring down presidents Dilma Rousseff and Lula da Silva.

**Sergio Moro and Glenn Greenwald's leaks**
Sergio Moro was the federal judge who led the Car Wash cases and convicted Lula in 2017, then became Bolsonaro's justice minister. In 2019, The Intercept Brasil, co-founded by American journalist Glenn Greenwald, published hacked messages showing Moro improperly coordinating with prosecutors; Brazil filed cybercrime charges against Greenwald in January 2020, which a judge later rejected. The hacker, Walter Delgatti Neto, later claimed Bolsonaro had asked him to try to hack voting machines.

**Jair Bolsonaro**
Far-right former army captain who was elected president in 2018 over Fernando Haddad and served until 2023. He made notorious remarks, such as that he would rather have a dead son than a gay one, praised the military dictatorship and its DOI-CODI secret police, promoted chloroquine during COVID-19 after catching the disease himself, and joked that the Pfizer vaccine could turn people into alligators or crocodiles.

**Impeachment of Dilma Rousseff**
Brazil's first female president, from the Workers' Party, who defeated Aécio Neves in 2014. She was impeached on charges of manipulating the federal budget and removed from office on August 31, 2016, in a Senate trial presided over by Supreme Court chief justice Ricardo Lewandowski; supporters called it a coup.

**Michel Temer**
Rousseff's vice president, who succeeded her in 2016. He was criticized for naming a cabinet made up entirely of white men, was secretly recorded in 2017 by JBS meatpacking executive Joesley Batista apparently discussing hush money for jailed politician Eduardo Cunha, and was depicted as a vampire by a samba school at the 2018 Rio Carnival. A 2015 letter he wrote to Rousseff complaining of being sidelined began with the Latin phrase "Verba volant, scripta manent."

**Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva**
Workers' Party leader who was president from 2003 to 2010 and was convicted of corruption in the Car Wash probe in 2017. Because he was jailed and barred from running in 2018, the party nominated former São Paulo mayor Fernando Haddad instead. Lula's convictions were later annulled, and he defeated Bolsonaro in the 2022 election to return to the presidency.

**Odebrecht**
A giant Brazilian construction conglomerate at the center of Operation Car Wash, which admitted to paying hundreds of millions of dollars in bribes to officials across Latin America. Its CEO, Marcelo Odebrecht, was arrested in 2015 and sentenced to prison.

**January 8, 2023 attacks in Brasília**
A week after Lula's inauguration, thousands of Bolsonaro supporters who refused to accept his 2022 election loss stormed and vandalized the National Congress, the Supreme Federal Court, and the presidential palace in Brasília. The event was widely compared to the January 6 attack on the U.S. Capitol.

**Eduardo Cunha**
The speaker of Brazil's Chamber of Deputies who opened impeachment proceedings against Dilma Rousseff in 2015. He was himself later removed from office, convicted of taking bribes connected to Petrobras, and jailed.

**Brazil vs. Germany 7–1 (Mineirazo)**
A 2014 World Cup semifinal held in Belo Horizonte's Mineirão stadium, in which host Brazil lost 7–1 to Germany; the humiliation is called the "Mineirazo" or "Agony of Mineirão." Miroslav Klose scored to become the all-time leading World Cup goalscorer, and Germany went on to win the title. The two countries also met in the 2002 final, where Ronaldo scored both goals in Brazil's 2–0 win against goalkeeper Oliver Kahn.

**2019 Amazon rainforest fires**
A surge of fires in the Amazon in 2019, mostly set to clear land for farming and ranching. Bolsonaro, who had weakened environmental enforcement, baselessly suggested that environmental nonprofits had started the fires to damage his government.

**Teori Zavascki**
The Supreme Federal Court justice overseeing the Car Wash cases, including the huge plea deals with Odebrecht executives. He died in a January 2017 plane crash off the coast of Rio de Janeiro state.

**Zika virus and the 2016 Rio Olympics**
A Zika virus outbreak in Brazil in 2015–2016 was linked to a sharp rise in babies born with microcephaly, a birth defect involving an abnormally small head. The outbreak raised fears ahead of the 2016 Summer Olympics, which were held in Rio de Janeiro.

**Carlos Ghosn**
A Brazilian-born businessman of Lebanese descent who led the Renault-Nissan alliance. He was arrested in Japan in 2018 on charges of financial misconduct, including underreporting his compensation, and was removed as Nissan chairman; in 2019 he fled to Lebanon while out on bail.

**Belo Monte Dam**
A huge and controversial hydroelectric dam on the Xingu River in the Amazonian state of Pará, Brazil's largest fully domestic dam and second in capacity only to the Itaipu Dam on the Paraguay border. It displaced tens of thousands of people, including Indigenous communities.
